issues.description: The problem statement's UML and method descriptions specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns an int, but the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object (and includes a StudentCount class). This creates a structural mismatch: students following the UML will expect an int return type and may implement or test against int, while the solution uses a custom wrapper type, which can cause confusion and incompatible signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the UML and problem description. Either change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (summing inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount wrapper, or update the problem statement/UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and document the StudentCount class. Ensure related methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents, getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor, and any tests) are updated accordingly.

issues.description: The concept 'total number of students' is represented inconsistently: the problem statement's UML and task description specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution introduces a new class StudentCount and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return StudentCount. This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) for the same conceptual entity expected as a primitive int and may confuse students about the expected return type and how to implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the total student count across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to return a primitive int from getTotalNumberOfStudents() (e.g., public int getTotalNumberOfStudents()) and remove or avoid using the StudentCount wrapper, or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the StudentCount wrapper type (and rename the UML return type accordingly) so students expect and understand the StudentCount class. Option A is recommended to match the original UML and reduce cognitive load.
